description.narrative: The objectives of the Ust-Kamenogorsk Environmental Remediation Project for Kazakhstan are to: (i) prevent the groundwater contamination plume's further migration towards the residential areas, the city's sources of drinking water supply and eventually into the Irtysh River; and (ii) strengthen institutional mechanisms for groundwater quality monitoring to enable control of ongoing groundwater pollution from local municipal and industrial sources. There are three components to the project, the first component being containment of high-priority sources of groundwater contamination; the second component is the remediation of current contaminated groundwater sites; and finally, the third component is the project management and monitoring. With respect to lessons drawn from prior experience in the region and sector, Bank experience has shown that: a) the need to coordinate among key government agencies and the concerned industries can present challenges that should be taken into account in the design of project implementation arrangements; b) local institutions need to be highly involved from the 10 earliest stages of the project; and c) competent and efficient national management staff are invaluable in ensuring the viability and sustainability of the project and should be brought on at an early stage.

The project has two development objectives: (i) Prevent the groundwater contamination plume's further migration towards the residential areas, the city's sources of drinking water supply and eventually into the Irtysh River; and (ii) Strengthen institutional mechanisms for groundwater quality monitoring to enable control of ongoing groundwater pollution from local municipal and industrial sources.

title.narrative: Reduce level of heavy metals & other hazardous pollutants in groundwater, thereby reducing risk of contamination of city's soil & groundwater system, drinking water wells, & surface water of Irtysh.

baseline.value: Based on the detailed one year monitoring campaign, there were no exceedings of maximum allowable concentrations have been detectedat the Oktyabrskiy drinking water well nor the wells surrounding the well. Neither local Kazakhstan drinking water MaximumAllowable Concentrations (MACs), nor the MACs specified by the International Guidelines for drinking water quality (established bythe World Health Organization) thus, the groundwater in and near Oktyabrskiy well-field nowadays is not contaminated.

target.value: Level of heavy metals pollution in groundwater reduced to below international limits.

actual.value:
No exceedings of maximum allowable concentrations have been detected near the drinking water well-field, neither local Kazakhstandrinking water Maximum Allowable Concentrations (MACs), nor the MACs specified by the International Guidelines for drinking waterquality (established by the World Health Organization) thus, the groundwater in Oktyabrskiy well-field nowadays is notcontaminated.
The concentration of harmful substances in the groundwater is higher in the close proximity to the territory of theCentral Industrial Complex and reduces moving away from the Central Industrial Complex. This is is proven by results obtained fromOskemen-Vodokanal drinking water wells and the 4th group of monitoring wells.(which are further away from the Central IndustrialComplex)
It was based on the detailed findings of the groundwater monitoring, that the groundwater pumping and treatment systemwas cancelled. The pollution in the groundwater and the migration of the pollution was not severe enough to justify such investmentand operating costs of such system, specifically since the risks of contamination of the drinking water wells and the Irtysh riverwas sufficiently low as the pollution was more immobilized near the Central Industrial Complex and did not migrate through thegroundwater system towards the drinking water wells and Irtysh river. However continued groundwater monitoring is required as thereare exceedences of pollutants in the groundwater.
For the key indicator under the Project, heavy metals, the results of the secondmonitoring campaign showed that Boron was the only metal which showed insignificant increases in the group of the 4th monitoringwells. The third monitoring campaign found only increased quantities of Selenium

title.narrative: Reduce level of heavy metals & other hazardous pollutants in groundwater, thereby reducing risk of contamination of city's soil & groundwater system, drinking water wells, & surface water of Irtysh.

baseline.value: Baseline data will be determined after completion of a 2 year detailed monitoring program and detail design has been prepared.

target.value: Level of heavy metals pollution in groundwater reduced to below international limits.

actual.value:
No exceedings of maximum allowable concentrations have been detected, neither local Kazakhstan drinking water Maximum AllowableConcentrations (MACs), nor the MACs specified by the International Guidelines for drinking water quality (established by the WorldHealth Organization) thus, the groundwater in Oktyabrskiy well-field nowadays is not contaminated.
The concentration of harmfulsubstances in the groundwater is significantly high in the close proximity to the territory of the Central Industrial Complex andgradually reduces afar, which is proven by results obtained from Oskemen-Vodokanal operating wells and the 4th group ofmonitoring wells.(further away from the Central Industrial Complex)
Exceedings of Maximum Allowable Concentrations in thegroundwater aquifer were found, especially for metals and inorganics, in their majority the obtained results showed that harmfulconcentrations even exceeded the WHOs Guidelines Values, which are less strict than RoK MACs;
Additionally, there are occurrenceswith Cadmium and Thallium in hydroposts (in the River) in December. This matter needs further thorough investigation in secondmonitoring round to bring light on the situation with such hazardous element
